While we love sports and we love beer, we most certainly aren't a traditional sports bar either, and we are so much more than just a classic Irish Channel watering hole. We're a part of Irish Channel history.
Located uptown on the world famous Magazine Street, The recently updated Rendezvous Tavern boasts over 80 beers, ciders and seltzers , 12 game TVs, billiards, darts, comedy, trivia, poker machines, unbeatable air conditioning, amazing food pop-ups and the cheapest drink prices in town

The Rendezvous boasts 12 big screen TVs, with MLB , NBA , NHL, and NFL TV packages located in all parts of the bar so you never miss your favorite team or an important game.

Best Beer Selection in New Orleans? Rendezvous Tavern! ?
We offer one of the biggest beer selections in New Orleans. We keep our beers at 32º to give you the best possible drinking experience. Don't see your favorite beer listed? Let us know !
Show All Fruited Gose Stout IPA THC Kölsch Wheat Ales Lagers Bock Low Calorie Non Alcoholic Ales Popular Dunkel On Tap Local Sour In a Bottle Malt Liquor In a Can Pilsners Ciders Rads-Shandy's Fruit Lambic Seltzers
NÜTRL Blueberry
Real vodka, real blueberry, real simple — just five ingredients and zero pretense. Gluten-free, crisp, and lightly sweet without tipping into candy. Smooth enough that the can's empty before you've decided whether you liked it, so you grab another just to be sure. Science, basically.
St. Arnold’s Ginger Beer
Non-alcoholic ginger beer with real bite — spicy, sharp, and aggressively fizzy. Great on its own when you're taking the night off, even better as the backbone of a mule. The designated driver's secret weapon, and nobody at the bar has to know it's booze-free.
Mich Ultra Zero
Zero carbs, zero sugar, zero guilt — and all the crisp, clean Michelob Ultra you already love. The gym-bro's post-workout trophy and the designated driver's best friend, poured ice cold. Basically water that gives you a buzz, and we mean that as a compliment.
Busch
No frills, no fuss, all value — the blue-mountain classic that drinks ice cold and never dents the wallet. It won't win any awards and it isn't trying to; it just wants to keep your night rolling for cheap. Honest, cold, and exactly our kind of beer.
Super Lyte Vodka-ade
Skinny little vodka lemonade with barely any calories and every bit of the fun. Light, fizzy, and just tart enough to stay interesting without the sugar crash. The one you reach for when you want to keep going but not keep score. Easy drinking, easy on tomorrow.
Surfside Blueberry/Lemonade
Blueberry lemonade with a vodka backbone — sweet, tart, and gone before you've noticed. It drinks like summer in a tallboy and hides its punch like a champ. Pace yourself, or don't; we're not your mom. Perfect for patio afternoons that quietly turn into patio evenings.
Surfside Tea/Lemonade
Vodka iced tea shakes hands with lemonade — basically the Arnold Palmer that went off to college and came back fun. Crushable, refreshing, and built for slow patio day-drinking. Smooth enough that you'll forget there's vodka in it, right up until you stand up too fast.
Rolling Rock
The little green bottle from Latrobe, PA — clean, extra-pale, and endlessly easy. It carries a cult following and a mysterious "33" on the label that nobody, not even the brewery, can fully explain. Order one, squint at the number, contemplate life. Cheap, cheerful, and weirdly iconic.
Coors Light
The Silver Bullet — cold, crisp, and about as fussy as a screen door. Rocky Mountain cheap thrills that turn a fun shade of blue when they're cold enough, because apparently we needed a beer to double as a thermometer. Drinks fast, judges no one, disappears quicker.
Parish SIPs Black Currant Sour
A puckery black currant sour from Louisiana's own Parish Brewing — tart, fruity, and bright as a NOLA afternoon. It's the happy place for sour lovers and a gateway drug for the sour-curious. Just enough pucker to wake you up without turning your face fully inside out.
Angry Orchard Cider
Crisp, semi-sweet apple cider on tap — gluten-free, refreshing, and easy drinking. The move when you want something that isn't beer but still means business. Tastes like fall no matter the month, which in New Orleans is basically a public service. Pairs with everything, judges nothing.
Abita Seasonal
Whatever the folks at Abita are brewing for the season, we've got it pouring — Louisiana's own, always rotating, always fresh. Could be a pecan ale, could be something wild; that's half the fun. Ask the bartender what's on and let them talk you into it. Local and proud.
St. Rains Mango
Juicy mango THC seltzer — all the fun of a cocktail with none of the tomorrow. Non-alcoholic, fast-acting, and dangerously easy drinking, so respect the buzz and start slow. Tastes like a beach vacation you didn't have to book. Consider it your chill button in a can.
St. Rains Pear
Crisp orchard pear in a can, infused with THC instead of alcohol — light, refreshing, and built for a mellow patio afternoon. All the good vibes, no hangover, gluten-free to boot. Sip it slow and let it sneak up on you; honestly, that's the whole point.
Crescent 9 Ginger Lemonade
Spicy-sweet ginger lemonade with a hemp-derived THC kick — non-alcoholic, gluten-free, and made right here in NOLA. The ginger keeps it lively while the buzz keeps it interesting. Sip slow, because this one sneaks up on you nice and easy. Local good times, zero hangover attached.
Crescent 9 Tropical
Local NOLA THC seltzer with a tropical fruit-punch pop — all the good-time buzz and none of the booze or the regret. Crescent Canna's finest: non-alcoholic, gluten-free, and dangerously smooth. Tastes like a vacation and hits like a mellow one, so pace yourself. Paradise in a can.
NÜTRL Lime
Crystal-clear hard seltzer with an honest hit of fresh-squeezed lime — no artificial funk, no cloying sweetness. The 4.5% corn-vodka base stays politely out of the way and lets the citrus run the show. Crisp, sessionable, and dangerously easy to keep ordering. Simple done right.
Woodchuck Hard Cider
One of the OGs of American cider — straightforward, crisp, and leaning sweet without going full candy apple. Gentle fizz, easy drinking, and a reliable pick when beer isn't calling and you want something fruit-forward. No wild funk, no fuss; just a solid cider that knows its lane.
Urban South Lime Gose
A proper Gose done right — hazy gold with a zesty key-lime punch, a whisper of sea salt, and a coriander hum underneath. The tartness is bright and refreshing rather than face-melting, which makes it weirdly thirst-quenching. Sour-curious? This is exactly where you start.
Lindeman’s Framboise
Belgium's gateway lambic — pours deep ruby with a pink head and smells like a raspberry-jam heist. Sweet and lush up front, with just enough tart, funky edge to prove it's the real deal. Dessert, drink, or both; we don't judge. Dangerously easy for something this fancy.
Heineken 0.0
Heineken's non-alcoholic twin, and a shockingly convincing one — same green-bottle aroma, same crisp bite, minus the buzz. Some folks swear they can't tell in a blind taste; others say the flavor ghosts on the swallow. Either way, it's the designated driver's dignity in a bottle.
Hofbräu Hefe Weizen

Superior Seafood & Oyster Bar embodies classic American sensibilities in its name, giving a clear indication that only the finest seafood is offered at this establishment- truth be told! Located on the corner of St. Charles and Napoleon Avenues, in the heart of Uptown New Orleans, provides a deeper sense of history and place, drawing inspiration from the rich cultural heritage and city’s origins- French, Creole, Southern, African, and more- to create its distinctive menu.

The restaurant’s location has historical significance. In the mid 1800s, military leaders in Spanish Louisiana, like Francisco Bouligny, developed streets connecting residential areas to the business district. Now known as St. Charles Avenue, it was named to honor Charles III, who was a Saint and former King of Spain. As a result, of naming an uptown-to-downtown street after a Spaniard they needed balance. Bouligny’s descendants named their north-south road Napoleon Avenue after Napoleon Bonaparte.

The 25-foot ceiling, large antique mirrors, European bistro chairs and clothed tables, oval oyster bar, and antique tiled ceiling enliven the restaurant as if you stepped in a popular brasserie in Paris. A selection of ruby red leather booths in the front of the restaurant provides a place for private conversations. The weathered tiled floor with mosaic borders, and the light from enormous 1930s reproduction bulbed lanterns falls into the room to complement the other motifs. All of these dominating features distinguish Superior Seafood & Oyster Bar from all other restaurants in New Orleans

CYRIL NEVILLE, the Uptown Ruler, brings a lifetime of dreams come true. This two-time grammy winning icon is brilliant and beautiful on stage and in his recorded work. In this new chapter of his creative life, Cyril levels up even more with new songs, a fresh perspective on his decares of performance worldwide and a determined eye on the future. As Quint Davis , fonder and head of the new Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival watching Mr. Neville perform at the 2025 Jazz Fest Congo Square Stage said,” He’s still got it.”
Cyril Neville is one of the founding fathers of the New Orleans signature funky soul, rock jazz sound that has influenced countless artists and entertained millions of fans over his 5-decade career. Mr. Neville is a vocalist, songwriter, percussionist, painter, cultural icon and activist who richly deserves his Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award.
Born in 1948 in New Orleans, the youngest of the Neville Brothers was raised in a musical household, with his brothers Aaron, Art and Charles all making waves on the local musical scene. Their uncle George Landry was Big Chief Jolly of the Wild Tchoupitoulas Mardi Gras Indian Tribe, and young Cyril cut his teeth singing and playing percussion with the group. At 19, he joined his brother’s band, Art Neville and the Neville Sounds, and released his first single a year later.
Art’s band soon merged into the seminal group, The Meters, with Cyril, guitarist Leo Nocentelli, bassist George Porter, Jr. and drummer Zigaboo Modeliste. Their early releases – the singles “Sissy Strut, “Look-A-Py-Py” and “Sophisticated Sissy,” as well as the Cabbage Alley and the Neville Brothers Fire on the Bayou have become classics, and their funky grooves built a foundation for a large swath of today’s American popular music. The Meter’s reputation was cemented when the Rolling Stones offered them an opening spot on their 1975 world tour.
Art and Cyril left The Meters in 1977, and with Aaron and Charles formed the Neville Brothers. For 35 years the group rocked audiences from Tipitinas in New Orleans to Taipei playing venues all over the world with their imminently danceable funk rock. Their recordings such as the Grammy-winning Yellow Moon and equally successful follow-up Brother’s Keeper have entered the canon of classic American Music. The Neville Brothers have received four nominations to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and hopefully one day will receive their long overdue flowers there.
One of Cyril’s current projects includes touring with his son’s band, Omari Neville and the Fuel, but he can also be heard performing with fellow Meter Goerge Porter, Jr, Trombone Shorty and his nephew Ivan Neville’s band Dumpstafunk.
Mr. Neville has had a number of other musical projects over the years, including The Endangered Species Band, and the Uptown All Stars as well as Swamp Funk. After Hurricane Katrina, bluesman Tab Benoit formed the supergroup Voice of the Wetlands to advocate for coastal protections with Cyril Neville front and center stage. Mr. Neville has also has also toured singing with the funk powerhouse Galactic. In 2011 Mr. Neville formed his own supergroup, Royal Southern Brotherhood, with Devon Allman, Mike Zito, Charlie Wooten and Yonrico Scott.
Mr. Neville has recorded with a Who’s Who of the rock world including Bob Dylan, Jimmy Buffett, Dr. John, Willie Nelson, Branford Marsalis, and Carlos Santana. He is a prolific writer, co-authoring songs with Bono, Allen Toussant, Trombone Shorty and Taj Mahal among many.
Mr. Neville has made a number of television appearances including Saturday Night Live, NCIS: New Orleans and HBO’s Treme. For many hears he also operated his own Endangered Species record label. Now he works closely with senior manager Lara Lavi and her production company Dreaming In Color Entertainment to release new music including his latest single “Lemonade,” co-written with and produced by renowned trumpet player Shamarr Allen releasing in July 2025.
Cyril Neville has collected many accolades over the course of his 50 years plus career, including a Grammy award for the song, “Healing Chant” from the 1989 album, Yellow Moon produced by Daniel Lanois. In 2017, The Neville Brothers received the Austin City Limits Lifetime Achievement Award and a year later, The Meters were honored with a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award.
Perhaps Mr. Neville’s greatest joy is singing, recording and performing with his son Omari Neville whose band Omari Neville and the Fuel tours as Omari’s backup band. With refreshed management and talent agency, Cyril Neville is highly prolific and unstoppable in this next phase of his career with new music releasing monthly for the army of fans of the Wild Tchoupitoulas, Meters, Uptown Ruler, Neville Brothers and fans of New Orleans music and culture.

THE QUINTESSENTIAL JAZZ CLUB OF NEW ORLEANS
Opened 7 DAYS A WEEK, 2Pm-2Am*
Located in the heart of the enchanted Faubourg Marigny, just steps away from the hustle and bustle of the French Quarter, The Spotted Cat has been and remains the local favorite for live New Orleans music ranging from Traditional and Modern Jazz, Blues, Funk, Klezmer, and so much more. Patrons are sure to enjoy listening to local musicians playing their hearts out!
SEE OUR WEEKLY CALENDAR FOR UPCOMING SHOWS!
Please see our FAQ page for any questions about scheduling or admission.
*Welcome to New Orleans. Opening, closing, and scheduled band times are subject to change without notice depending on (but not limited to) parades, hurricanes (natural & man-made), second-lines, festivals, and music that is sometimes just too good to stop!
Read More Reviews!
What folks are saying about The Spotted Cat!
“ Great little place on Frenchmen Street, removed from the crowds and chaos of Bourbon Street. Bartenders were lively and friendly, pouring good drinks at reasonable prices. Meschiya Lake and the Little Big Horns played some of the best music we heard in NOLA. ”
- ★★★★★ Rhonda H. of Panama City, FL
“ Hands down, twas the best jazz bar I went to in New Orleans. Located on Frenchmen St where there’s plenty of jazz to go around twice, it’s small and intimate but by no means tame... unlike anything I’ve ever heard before - and as a piano player I can assure you the pianist was a genius. Every single one of them was! ”
- ★★★★★ Linda W. of Los Angeles, CA
“ Amazing place. Definitely on my top 3 best places in the city. I like the environment and music. Musicians are very nice and after each song one person goes around the place to collect donations. So if you’re shy or somewhere in the back - no worries. They got your money. Try come on Friday night they have pretty cool dancers/couples who will dance swing. The place is small but it has another huge plus compare to most other places on Frenchman. It’s their air conditioning! Very cool place! ”
- ★★★★★ Kirill V. of Manhattan, NY
“ In New Orleans but want to stay away from the drunken frat boys and girls gone wild? Looking for a real jazz club with a great atmosphere? I was in New Orleans for a conference and a friend suggested going to The Spotted Cat Music Club. It was packed for a reason. This small music box has a stage, bar, and a cozy jazz friendly area to stand and meet music lovers in a ‘locals’ area of the French Quarter. The talent is top notch and perhaps the key indicator of why this place is a local favourite.
I don’t give out a whole lot of 5 stars... the Spotted Cat Music Club deserves every one. ”
- ★★★★★ Kevin Y. of Toronto, Canada
